_headline: EUROSTAT'S OWN METADATA PAGE STATES A DOCUMENTED DEPENDENCY BETWEEN TWO NAMED EU STATISTICAL PRODUCTS: 'Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data.' That is the closest thing to a genuine EU-internal statistics-to-statistics edge this branch has found -- every prior EU finding has been about the asymmetry between the supranational and national layers, not a dependency running entirely within the EU statistical system itself.
_open_questions: DOMAIN GAP, same shape as the institutional-budget nodes' fiscal-transfers placeholder. Research.1.md 6's Domain union has no 'agriculture' or 'statistics' value. 'population' is used here as least-wrong -- the Farm Structure Survey is structurally a census/structural-survey instrument (it runs on a 10-year agricultural-census cycle explicitly modelled on population censuses, per its own preamble's reference to the FAO World Programme for the Census of Agriculture), which is a closer analogy than any of national-accounts, labour, or the fiscal/benefits domains. Flagged rather than assumed correct; extend the union at the other end if a better fit is wanted.

CADENCE is a genuine number this time, not a guess, but it changed regime partway through the record. Historically (1989/90 through 2016) reference years averaged roughly one every 2.6 years. Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 fixes the current regime at exactly 2020, 2023, 2026 -- a flat 3-year interval -- with dissemination stated as '2 years after the reference year' (a publication lag, not a frequency). releases_per_year is set to 0.33 to match the current, legally-fixed regime rather than the longer historical average; if a future session weights the full 1966-2026 run instead, the number would come out closer to 0.4.

reports.title: Farm Structure Survey (FSS)
reports.description: Eurostat's recurring survey of the structure of agricultural holdings across the EU, run in one form or another since 1966. Eurostat's own metadata page states: 'The data describe the structure of agricultural holdings providing the general characteristics of farms and farmers and information on their land, livestock and labour force. They also describe production methods, rural development measures and agro-environmental aspects... The aggregated results are disseminated through statistical tables.' Legally re-founded by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 ('on integrated farm statistics'), which fixed the current data collections at reference years 2020, 2023 and 2026 -- a census in 2020, sample surveys in 2023 and 2026 -- each covering at least 98% of the EU's utilised agricultural area and livestock units. Eurostat's own metadata states the FSS 'provid[es] a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data' -- see _dropped.
reports.cadence_note: Currently fixed at reference years 2020, 2023, 2026 by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 Article 5 -- a 3-year interval, with results 'disseminated 2 years after the reference year' (Eurostat metadata page, 'Frequency of dissemination'). Historically (1989/1990 through 2016) reference years averaged roughly one every 2.6 years on a 10-year agricultural-census cycle with 2-3 intermediate sample surveys between censuses. See _open_questions.

release_schedule.rule: Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, Article 5: 'Member States shall collect and provide the core structural data ... for the reference years 2020, 2023 and 2026.' Article 12 sets Member State transmission deadlines of 12 months after the end of the 2023/2026 reference years (15 months for 2020). Eurostat's own metadata for this dataset (ef_sims.htm, Accuracy/Timeliness section) states: 'Results are disseminated 2 years after the reference year.'
release_schedule.note: FSS is run on a 3-year cycle mandated by Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 (reference years 2020 [census], 2023, 2026); the regulation as currently in force does not specify years beyond 2026. As of the current date (2026-08-11) the 2026 reference-year survey is the cycle underway; per Eurostat's own metadata, results for a given reference year are disseminated about 2 years later, so 2026-reference-year results are expected around 2028 (exact month not published). This matches the releases_per_year=0.33 (~once every 3 years) already on file.

reports.title: Farm Sustainability Data Network (FSDN)
reports.publisher: European Commission (Directorate-General for Agriculture and Rural Development)
reports.description: The EU's annual farm-level accountancy and sustainability survey, and the other end of the one genuine EU-internal statistics-to-statistics edge this branch has found. DG AGRI's own page describes it as "an EU survey that gathers annual data about farms" which has "collected farm economics data from an annual sample of around 75 000 farms across the EU for more than 60 years", a sample that "represents 3.5 million farms and 90% of the EU's agricultural production". Selected through national liaison agencies from market-oriented farms. Its outputs are a public database of aggregated results, farm-economy dashboards at EU, country and sector level, and analytical briefs. RENAMED, and the old name is the one most documents still use: this is the former Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN), renamed and re-scoped by Regulation (EU) 2023/2674 amending Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009. As of 2025 the collection expanded beyond economics to "environmental and social sustainability performance", including quantities of fertilizers, pesticides, feed and antimicrobials. Current implementing instruments named on DG AGRI's page: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 (variable definitions, farm selection methodology, data-sharing), Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1417 (income determination and sustainability analysis) and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2499. Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) caps the sample: "the maximum number of returning holdings shall be 105 000 for the Community". MINTED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass). The blocker recorded in this file's `_open_questions` and `_dropped` was site access, and it is gone: agriculture.ec.europa.eu served both the FADN and FSDN pages as ordinary fetchable HTML this session, so the title, cadence, sample and URL now come from the network's own authoritative site rather than only from the legal instruments.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, stated as such by DG AGRI ("an annual sample of around 75 000 farms", "gathers annual data about farms"). Note this is the cadence of the data collection; the dashboards and analytical briefs built on it are published on their own schedules, which were not established this session.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY BY THIS SESSION (2026-08-09) -- Eurostat's 'Farm structure (ef)' metadata page re-fetched first-hand, and the sentence now pinned to its section: it sits in section 3.4, Statistical concepts and definitions. "Both the censuses and the sample surveys are aimed at producing a variety of information on specific CAP targets, as well as providing a basis for extrapolating Farm Accountancy Data Network (FADN) data." Direction is FSDN -> FSS, as the original lead reasoned: a ~75 000-farm sample capped by Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 5(3) at "105 000 for the Community" needs a population framework to extrapolate to the 3.5 million farms it claims to represent, and this record says the FSS supplies it. Typed `methodology_depends_on` rather than `uses_data_from`: what passes is a weighting/extrapolation framework, not FSS observations feeding into FSDN records. TWO CAVEATS, both stated rather than smoothed over. First, the evidence is ONE-SIDED: it is Eurostat asserting what its survey is used for, and DG AGRI's own FSDN page -- read in full this session -- names neither the Farm Structure Survey, nor integrated farm statistics, nor Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, nor Eurostat anywhere. The producer of the dependent product has not been found stating the dependency. Second, the quoted sentence still says FADN, the network's pre-2023 name; the node is minted under its current name, FSDN, so the edge crosses a rename. Nothing found this session suggests the extrapolation arrangement itself changed with the rename, but nothing found confirms it either -- a successor should look for the same statement in FSDN-era methodology (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 is the obvious place, since DG AGRI's page says it carries the farm-selection methodology).

CORROBORATED FROM THE RECEIVING SIDE, 2026-08-09 (closing G.64.md cheap check 3 / this file's own _open_questions item 4). The first caveat above -- that only Eurostat, the supplying side, had been found stating this dependency -- no longer holds. FSDN's own implementing regulation, Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2746 of 25 October 2024 ('laying down rules for the application of Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 setting up the Farm Sustainability Data Network...'), fetched directly from EUR-Lex (CELEX:32024R2746), states in Annex III ('Models and methods for selection plan preparation'): 'all relevant types and sizes of farming represented in the integrated farm statistics (IFS) census or survey are to be covered at the level of detail which provides representative results on important farm groups, within the limits of the sample size.' 'Integrated farm statistics' is the Farm Structure Survey's own legal name -- Regulation (EU) 2018/1091, which this node's own description cites as its re-founding instrument, is titled 'on integrated farm statistics'. Recital (5) of 2024/2746 cross-references the same instrument directly: 'These standard outputs need to be established by product and should align with the list of core structural data variables set out in Annex III to Regulation (EU) 2018/1091 of the European Parliament and of the Council.' So the FSDN sample-selection methodology names the FSS/IFS census as the population it must represent, on its own side of the relationship, independent of Eurostat's own metadata page. The second caveat (the edge crosses FADN's rename to FSDN) is unaffected -- 2024/2746 is itself an FSDN-era instrument and does not use the name FADN, so it does not help there either way.

_dropped.edge: European Commission annual report on the situation of agriculture and farm incomes -> (no target; the report itself was the candidate node)
_dropped.why: A DOCUMENTED CHANGE, NOT ADJUDICATED. As originally codified in 2009, Council Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 Article 1(3) required: 'The data obtained pursuant to this Regulation shall, in particular, serve as the basis for the drawing up of reports by the Commission on the situation of agriculture and of agricultural markets as well as on farm incomes in the Community. The reports shall be submitted annually to the European Parliament and the Council, in particular for the annual fixing of prices of agricultural produce.' That is AGENCY ONLY under Research.1.md 6 (no title given for the reports) but otherwise the cleanest annual-report obligation found anywhere in the EU branch. Regulation (EU) 2023/2674 replaced Article 1 in full; the replacement text (read directly, first-hand) contains no equivalent clause -- in its place, a duty to 'make the results of those analyses publicly available in the form of aggregated and anonymised FSDN data', with no stated cadence. Whether the annual-report duty survives elsewhere in the current consolidated text of Regulation (EC) No 1217/2009 was not checked; only the amending regulation's own replacement text was read. NOT MINTED on either reading: the 2009 version because it names no title, the 2023 version because it states no cadence. Full quotes in EU/FSDN_FSS_PartA_2026-08-05.md, records FSDN-01 and FSDN-02.
